forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-YES. Pakistani PM Sharif announced text agreement on the Islamabad MOU on June 12, 2026. US Vice President Vance confirmed the MOU was signed June 14-17. The Pakistan-mediated process constitutes a held mediated session between named US and Iranian principals, satisfying the resolution_source_rule's State Dept statement clause before the June 16 EOD deadline. Resolution confirmed via VP Vance's announcement and TIER1 corroboration.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement (MFA/state media IRNA/Tasnim/Fars) rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension. A held mediated session counts; mere rhetorical assertion that 'talks continue' or relay of written messages does NOT count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Iranian MFA spokesman confirms re-engagement or rescinds suspension
Omani/Qatari mediator readout of a convened/held session

forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a face-to-face or formally convened indirect negotiating session between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, hosted by a named mediator (Oman/Pakistan/Qatar), between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Axios/Al Jazeera/Times of Israel; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also qualifies.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Mere relay of written messages, or one side asserting talks 'continue' without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange — Israeli strikes on Iranian targets AND Iranian strikes on Israeli/Israeli-claimed targets — within any rolling 48h window between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera) OR one TIER1 + official Israeli (IDF) or Iranian (IRGC) statement.

forecasts.question: Will Hormuz reach >=50 commercial transits/day (7-day avg) before EOD 2026-07-02?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. Strait of Hormuz remained effectively closed through the June-July window. Only 1 commercial vessel transited on August 9, 2026 versus ~73/day pre-war (Lloyd's List Intelligence). The best-documented recent 7-day window (July 27-Aug 2) recorded ~84 total transits = ~12/day, still 76% below the 50/day threshold. No evidence of any 7-day window approaching 50 transits during June-July.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if IMF PortWatch (or equivalent AIS) records >=50 commercial transits/day averaged over any consecutive 7-day window between 2026-06-02 and 2026-07-02.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IMF PortWatch + one TIER1/OSINT shipping report (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd's List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval-escorted convoys count; one-off surge days below a 7-day window do NOT qualify; if PortWatch unpublished, use best AIS tracker and flag AMBIGUOUS if sources conflict >20%.

indicators.name: PortWatch 7-day transit trend rising
P&I war-risk cover reinstated for Hormuz transit

forecasts.question: Will the Knesset pass the dissolution bill's final reading with a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27 before EOD 2026-07-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO (dual failure). Ground 1: Knesset dissolution bill final reading occurred July 17, 2026 — two days after the July 15 EOD deadline. Ground 2: Election date set for exactly October 27, 2026 (the legally mandated last possible date); the ambiguity rule explicitly states 'if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.' Judge design-failure note: the strict-less-than operator (< Oct 27) created a no-resolution trap for the most probable real-world outcome; future Israeli political forecasts should use ≤ and account for ±72h Knesset scheduling slippage.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the Knesset passes the dissolution bill in final (third) reading AND that passage specifies a fixed election date earlier than 2026-10-27, before EOD 2026-07-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two TIER1 (Times of Israel/Reuters/AP/JPost) citing the Knesset plenum vote record.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Preliminary/first/second readings without final passage do NOT count; passage that leaves the date to a later committee or sets only a band without a fixed date = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; if a fixed date on/after 27 Oct is set, resolve NO.

indicators.name: Plenum third-reading dissolution vote held with a fixed date inserted

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RETIRED-OBE. Events have superseded the question entirely. The Knesset completed its full term and formally dissolved July 17, 2026 by a 62-0 self-directed vote — the first full-term Knesset since 1988. The coalition held a bare 61-seat majority through the caretaker period (Shas formally resigned from government posts but nominally remained in coalition; UTJ departed earlier during Haredi crisis). The question cannot resolve under its own criteria: no formal majority-loss roll-call vote occurred, and the election date is exactly Oct 27 — not 'earlier than Oct 27' as the resolution criteria requires. The question's underlying uncertainty (Netanyahu's political survival) has been subsumed by the confirmed election calendar. Replaced by new F7 tracking the Oct 27 election outcome directly.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.

indicators.name: Smotrich formally departs coalition
Degel HaTorah files formal dissolution motion in Knesset

forecasts.question: Will the US-Iran Islamabad MOU ceasefire be publicly confirmed as extended — by a named US, Iranian, or Pakistani official — before EOD 2026-08-17?
forecasts.delta_reason: Judge-calibrated at 0.55, mediating between Analyst proposal (0.65) and DA assessment (0.50). Pakistani Interior Minister Naqvi arrived Tehran Aug 13 carrying a 'special and important message' from PM Sharif; Naqvi-Araghchi talks confirmed by multiple Pakistani outlets as active Aug 12-13. One indicator (Pakistani mediation) is PARTIAL. However, Iran's FM publicly told state media the channel is 'messages through intermediaries' not negotiations; no US statement; no joint communiqué; extension duration (60 or 90 days) not finalized. DA's MOU-void contradiction concern accepted: ABC News documented MOU breakdown pattern; US reimposed naval blockade in August. 55% reflects active high-level mediation with meaningful but not dominant probability of public confirmation in 3 days.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if named US official (SecState/NSA/CENTCOM commander/president), named Iranian official (FM/MFA spokesperson/president), or Pakistani government formally confirms MOU extension in public statement — OR both sides issue joint mediator communiqué — before EOD 2026-08-17.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1 (Reuters, AP, AFP, Al Jazeera) or official US/Iran/Pakistan government communiqué. Single-source claim from Pakistan Today or similar regional outlet does not suffice; requires TIER1 or government-level attribution.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Aug 17 passes with no statement from any party but no new confirmed US-Iran direct strikes: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO pending mediator clarification within 48h. Extension 'understood' or 'expected' per unnamed sources only = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: Pakistani PM/FM formal public statement on MOU extension duration
Iran FM Araghchi no longer publicly denying ceasefire continues
US State Dept or White House confirms ongoing ceasefire framework

forecasts.question: Will Iran and Oman sign and publicly release a formal written framework agreement on Strait of Hormuz commercial transit management before EOD 2026-09-07?
forecasts.delta_reason: Deputy FM Gharibabadi (IRNA, Aug 5) said the Iran-Oman agreement is 'finalizing' after three weeks of talks with four working groups established (sanctions, nuclear, reconstruction, monitoring). Fortune reported Aug 7 that 'Iran says agreement on Strait of Hormuz shipping reached.' However, no Omani confirmation of a signed document has been published, and Iran explicitly warned the deal 'will not automatically reopen the waterway' pending US lifting of its naval blockade — a condition the US has not met. DA opposing narrative accepted: the MOU-void contradiction applies here too; a signed framework without US compliance on the naval blockade is a document without operational effect.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a formal written joint statement or agreement signed by named Iranian and Omani FM-level officials is publicly released, covering commercial transit arrangements for the Strait of Hormuz — before EOD 2026-09-07. Minimum: both sides must confirm the document's existence on the record.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1 (Reuters, AP, AFP) or official Iranian MFA communiqué confirmed by Omani MOFA or TIER1 Omani source. Iran-only claim without Omani corroboration = insufficient.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Verbal announcement only without published document = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; draft framework leaked but unsigned = NO; deal announced but key provisions (US naval blockade, sovereignty) explicitly deferred to later stage = AMBIGUOUS.

indicators.name: Iran FM or Deputy FM declares talks concluded with a signed and released document
US announces partial suspension or modification of Iranian port blockade

forecasts.question: Will the Strait of Hormuz 7-day rolling average of daily commercial transits reach or exceed 25 vessels per day at any point before EOD 2026-09-07?
forecasts.delta_reason: Current transit: 1 vessel on August 9 (Lloyd's List Intelligence) versus approximately 73 per day pre-crisis. MOU's operational peak (mid-June to July 7) produced only approximately 28 vessels per day before the framework collapsed and the US naval blockade was reimposed. As of August 14: US naval blockade fully active; US fired on a Panama-flagged cargo ship attempting to breach the blockade; Iran has not agreed to reopen the strait; war-risk insurance markets remain closed to Hormuz transits. Reaching 25 per day within 24 days requires Iran to announce reopening AND the US to at least suspend blockade for commercial traffic AND insurance markets to clear. All three conditions are unmet. DA opposing narrative fully accepted for this forecast: p=0.18 is consistent with the DA's constraint that de-escalation probability for 30-day Hormuz reopening should remain below 0.30.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if any TIER1 maritime data provider (Lloyd's List Intelligence, UANI, Xinde Marine News, or IMF Hormuz tracker) reports a 7-day trailing average of at least 25 commercial transits per day at any point before EOD 2026-09-07. Warships, IRGC vessels, and Iranian-flagged vessels excluded from the commercial transit count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Lloyd's List Intelligence Hormuz Brief, UANI shipping updates, or Statista/IMF data; or TIER1 confirming AIS aggregator data from any named provider. Requires named data source, not news estimate.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Multiple primary data providers showing conflicting figures spanning the 25-per-day threshold: AMBIGUOUS pending 48h resolution. If primary provider shows below 25 but news reports claim above, primary data provider governs.

forecasts.question: Will Iranian-backed forces (Houthis, Iraqi PMF, or other IRGC-directed groups) carry out an attack inside Saudi Arabia causing at least 5 fatalities or confirmed destruction of primary energy infrastructure before EOD 2026-09-07?
forecasts.delta_reason: Houthis claimed a drone strike on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on August 9 — Saudi Arabia has not independently confirmed refinery damage. Saudi intelligence sources warned Al Arabiya (Aug 6-7) of imminent coordinated attacks from Iraqi PMF (north) and Houthis (south) on Saudi civilian and energy sites. Iran's military command reportedly ordered a 'more aggressive' posture for a protracted-conflict scenario per a Pentagon assessment (ZeroHedge, Aug 9). The August 7 Mecca Joint Defense Agreement (Turkey-Saudi-Pakistan) introduces a marginal deterrence factor, but Houthi operational tempo has accelerated irrespective of diplomatic developments. Historical base rate from Houthi-Saudi operations: confirmed infrastructure damage roughly once per four to six weeks. Houthi indicator PARTIAL (spokesperson announced dedicated Saudi operations).
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if TIER1 confirms at least 5 fatalities from a single incident attributed to Houthis, Iraqi PMF, or IRGC-directed group on Saudi territory — OR confirmed total loss of primary function of a named energy facility (refinery, pipeline, pumping station, or LNG terminal) — before EOD 2026-09-07. Drone harassment causing minor damage or zero casualties = NO. Strikes on Saudi naval vessels in international waters = NO.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters, AP, or Saudi SPA for fatality claims; ACLED event data or Lloyd's List for infrastructure confirmation. Houthi claims alone without Saudi or TIER1 corroboration do not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Attack occurs but attribution disputed by Saudi government OR casualty count unverified by a second source after 72h: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO pending independent confirmation.

forecasts.question: Will IAEA inspectors physically verify access to at least one Iranian declared nuclear facility and publicly report findings before EOD 2026-09-14?
forecasts.delta_reason: IAEA inspectors have had no physical access to Iranian declared nuclear facilities since June 2025. Iran's stockpile stands at approximately 440.9kg of 60%-enriched UF6 (unverified per IAEA as of last verified inspection). The June 17 MOU included a nuclear inspection clause within the 60-day negotiating period, but no IAEA access was confirmed before the MOU's contested expiry. Iran's FM Araghchi explicitly links IAEA access to US compliance with MOU provisions — specifically ending the naval blockade of Iranian ports and Persian Gulf access. The 31-day window is short for bridging this gap, and the MOU ceasefire extension itself (F1) is uncertain as of Aug 14.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the IAEA Director-General or Board of Governors officially confirms that inspectors physically entered and conducted verification activities at a named Iranian declared nuclear facility before EOD 2026-09-14. Remote monitoring (cameras or seals) without physical inspector presence = NO. Iranian verbal assurance of future access without IAEA confirmation = NO.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IAEA official press releases or Board of Governors reports; or TIER1 quoting IAEA Director-General Grossi or Deputy DG for Safeguards by name with attribution on confirmed access.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Inspectors enter Iran but access limited to non-declared or newly agreed sites not on the safeguards list: AMBIGUOUS pending IAEA characterization that visit fulfills safeguards verification. Iran announces IAEA visit but IAEA does not confirm: NO.

indicators.name: IAEA DG Grossi publicly announces access negotiation concluded with confirmed timeline

forecasts.question: Will a TIER1-confirmed formal US-Iran negotiating session — with named delegation leads physically present or simultaneously on video conference — occur before EOD 2026-10-27?

Iran's preconditions (end US naval blockade, honor MOU) are demanding but not structurally impossible to partially meet given the Mecca Pact's new regional diplomacy context. Base rate: approximately one formal Pakistan-mediated session per 60-90 days since the April 2026 breakthrough.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if TIER1 confirms a formal negotiating session — named US envoy AND named Iranian official in the same physical location OR simultaneous video conference — with Pakistan, Oman, or Qatar as mediator physically present. Electronic message exchange or written communications relayed by mediators only = NO.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: TIER1 (Reuters, AP, BBC, Washington Post, New York Times) or official government readout from any participating state (US, Iran, Pakistan, Oman, or Qatar).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Session occurs but Iran characterizes it as a 'technical meeting' or 'mediator consultation' rather than bilateral negotiation AND no mediator confirms bilateral character of the session: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party finish with the most seats among all individual parties in the October 27, 2026 Israeli legislative election?
forecasts.delta_reason: Polls August 9-11: Likud at 22-24 seats; Yashar (Eisenkot-led) at approximately 24-25 seats per Haaretz. The August 11 Haaretz poll places the Eisenkot-led bloc at 60 seats collectively — one seat short of a working majority without Arab parties. Netanyahu recovered Likud from earlier lows in the August 9 poll (recovering to 24 seats, matching Eisenkot), but net approval on war handling remains negative in most surveys. The 74-day campaign window allows for significant polling movement. The Iran war's trajectory — specifically the August 17 MOU expiry (F1) and any developments before election day — is the dominant swing variable for Likud's standing.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if official results certified by Israel's Central Elections Committee show Likud with the highest individual-party seat total in the October 27, 2026 election. Ties: if Likud shares first place with any other party at exactly equal seats, resolve YES only if Likud is listed first in the official certification.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israel's Central Elections Committee (HaVaada HaMerkazit LaBchirot) official results; or TIER1 reporting of final certified count. Exit polls or preliminary partial counts do not resolve the forecast.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Top two parties finish within 1 seat and a recount or legal challenge is underway: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO pending final certification. If election is postponed beyond Oct 27, forecast extends to the rescheduled date.
